title: Edmonton's Sneha Joy Wins $5 Million Lotto 6/49 Jackpot
excerpt: Joy matched all six numbers in the October 21 Classic draw with a ticket bought on the Lotto Spot app, and plans to clear her mortgage, travel the world and share with family.
body:
• Edmonton's Sneha Joy matched all six numbers — 1, 10, 18, 22, 33 and 37 — in the October 21 Lotto 6/49 Classic draw to win $5 million.
  • The Western Canada Lottery Corporation announced the win this week; Joy bought the winning ticket through the Lotto Spot app and plays regularly.
  • "I was shocked," Joy said while claiming her prize, describing the best part of winning as being "financially stress-free."
  • Her stated plans are concrete: pay off her mortgage, travel around the world, and share the winnings with family and loved ones.

An Edmonton woman who plays Lotto 6/49 regularly is $5 million richer. Sneha Joy matched all six numbers in the October 21 Lotto 6/49 Classic draw, the Western Canada Lottery Corporation announced this week, in a win first reported by the Edmonton Journal.

The winning ticket

Joy's ticket carried the numbers 1, 10, 18, 22, 33 and 37, matching all six in the Classic draw, whose jackpot is fixed at $5 million. She purchased the ticket through the Lotto Spot app, according to lottery officials. "I was shocked," Joy said while claiming her prize, adding that she felt a mix of happiness and relief, and describing the best part of winning as being "financially stress-free."

"I was shocked."

— Sneha Joy, on claiming her prize

What she plans to do with it

Joy's plans, as reported by the Journal and summarized by Khojipedia from the lottery corporation's release, are specific rather than extravagant: pay off her mortgage first, then take a trip around the world, and share the winnings with her family and loved ones — which she said matters as much to her as her own goals.

One of several Alberta wins this year

Joy is one of several Albertans to win a $5 million Lotto 6/49 jackpot this year, a reminder of how the Classic draw's fixed prize produces a steady run of identical headline wins. What sets this one apart for diaspora readers is the shape of the plan: clear the mortgage, see the world, and take family along in the proceeds — in that order.
